text: If he did not murder his wife, he is, nevertheless, a scoundrel, and has something of his own to conceal, quite apart from the murder.” “What can it be?” I mused, won over to Poirot’s views for the moment, although still retaining a faint conviction that the obvious deduction was the correct one. “Can you not guess?” asked Poirot, smiling. “No, can you?” “Oh, yes, I had a little idea sometime ago—and it has turned out to be correct.” “You never told me,” I said reproachfully. Poirot spread out his hands apologetically. “Pardon me, mon ami, you were not precisely sympathique.” He turned to me earnestly.
